title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 50 (Company to Accept Unpaid Share Capital, Although Not Called Up)

content.overview: Section 50(1) provides that a company may, if so authorised by its articles, accept from any member the whole or a part of the amount remaining unpaid on any shares held by him, even if no part of that amount has been called up. Section 50(2) provides that a member of the company limited by shares shall not be entitled to any voting rights in respect of the amount paid by him under sub-section (1) until that amount has been called up.
content.glance: If articles authorise, company may accept unpaid capital in advance of calls; no voting rights on that amount until it has been called up.
content.study: A company may, if so authorised by its articles, accept from any member the whole or a part of the amount remaining unpaid on any shares held by him, even if no part of that amount has been called up (s. 50(1)). A member of the company limited by shares shall not be entitled to any voting rights in respect of the amount paid by him under sub-section (1) until that amount has been called up (s. 50(2)). Current-law framing: check articles authorisation; identify voluntary payment in advance of calls; deny voting rights on that sum until it has been called up.

sections.heading: Power to accept (s. 50(1))
sections.body: If authorised by the articles, the company may accept from a member the whole or part of the amount remaining unpaid on any shares held by him, even if no part of that amount has been called up.

sections.heading: No voting until called up (s. 50(2))
sections.body: A member of a company limited by shares shall not be entitled to any voting rights in respect of the amount paid under sub-section (1) until that amount has been called up.

provisions.title: Company to accept unpaid share capital, although not called up

examples.title: Payment in advance
examples.body: Articles authorise acceptance of unpaid capital. A member pays the remaining unpaid amount on partly paid shares before any call. Section 50 applies; no voting rights on that amount until it has been called up.

examples.title: No articles authority
examples.body: Articles are silent. The company cannot rely on s. 50 without articles authorisation.

hypotheticals.question: Does payment in advance of calls give immediate extra voting power?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 50(2) denies voting rights in respect of such moneys until that amount has been called up.

distinctions.title: Acceptance of unpaid capital (s. 50) vs uniform calls (s. 49)
distinctions.left: Voluntary payment in advance of calls
distinctions.right: Company-initiated calls on a uniform class basis

misconceptions.trap: Paying in advance automatically increases voting power.
misconceptions.correction: Section 50(2) denies voting rights on amounts paid in advance until that amount has been called up.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 50 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Check articles authorisation. II. Identify payment in advance of calls. III. Apply no-voting rule until the amount has been called up. IV. Conclude.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Articles; payment facts; voting claim if any; precise relief.

examTips: No voting on advance payments until the amount has been called up.
